item.title: MOD: Kappa in Super Metroid
item.author: engineerkappa@gmail.com (Anna Sandlin)
item.description:
I love Super Metroid, I love Randomizers, and I love making sprites of my little goobers. I thought it would be fun making sprites of my goober to play as in Super Metroid randomizers.

...Unfortunately at the time of writing this my controllers are still in storage, so testing this means enduring Super Metroid on keyboard.

Download

Sprite Sheet Download

I recommend using SpriteSomething to inject the sprite sheet into the rom of your choice. I've only tested it with the vanilla game and Map Rando, but in theory it should work with other randomizers.

Things to Note

  • Kappa's short. Their gun's way lower than Samus's and there isn't really any way to get around that. Maybe it'd be cool one day making a proper hack someday affecting all the shot positions and hitboxes.
  • There are some minor animation misalignments, mostly just things Super Metroid already does that are hard to work around.

item.title: What the heck is an RSS?
item.author: engineerkappa@gmail.com (Anna Sandlin)
item.description:
Everyone knows social media sucks, so I'm not going to waste your time ranting about why you'd want other options. One of those other options is RSS, a standard format for aggregating content across the internet. At least that's what I think it does?

This format feels prehistoric, and yet I've never once interacted with it. Apparently Hugo, the web framework I use, has native support for it? Maybe I should actually mess with that some?

It's hard to tailor my content for a format I don't really even use...

Do I need to format things in a specific way? I might have to. I'll let y'all know what I find.

Update from a few hours later: Managed to clean the feed somewhat! Should have better metadata, utility pages like the sitemap shouldn't be included in the feed anymore.

item.title: Web Dev is Hard
item.author: engineerkappa@gmail.com (Anna Sandlin)
item.description:
Do you ever encounter a task that's kind of tedious, and you realize you know some way to make it go faster, only to spend way longer automating it than it would've taken in the first place?

Hi, this is the programmer bunny speaking!

The site you're reading here is written in Hugo. Hugo is a tool/ framework/ thingamajig that lets you generate static HTML from Markdown files, manage content formatting, and some other things I don't feel like getting into.

We just spent Way too long trying to set our site up, so ideally this should be easier to update now? Dump a blog post or two on here when we're feeling it. Hopefully.

Still can't help but wonder if it would've been easier gritting our teeth and writing raw HTML to do these things. Who knows. This is just a single markdown file we have to edit, and it automatically gets linked elsewhere on the site.

What else will we post here?

It is a mystery!
